answers.why: Israel's families collectively become the LORD's people.
Israel is identified as the people who survived the sword.
The virgin Israel personifies the nation restored to rejoicing and planting vineyards.
The remnant of Israel is explicitly called God's people and gathered from exile.
God calls himself Israel's father while leading the returning company of exiles.
Ephraim is God's figurative firstborn in the restoration of the exiled people.
Israel is the scattered people whom God gathers and guards like a flock.
Ephraim personifies the chastised people whose children will return to their territory.
God describes repentant Ephraim as a dear child before calling Israel back to its cities.
The virgin Israel is summoned to return to its cities.
The God of Israel promises restoration from captivity to the nation's land and cities.
Judah and its cities are inhabited by farmers and shepherds after restoration.
Israel's continuing offspring are explicitly described as a nation before God.
Israel's offspring are the enduring national community whose deeds God addresses.
